title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
claim: Raising lanthanide nuclearity multiplies structural motifs but makes magneto-structural control harder because metal-metal interactions grow much more complex than in binuclear analogues.
explanation: The review notes linear, sawtooth, and polyhedral architectures as nuclearity increases, and states that interaction complexity rises exponentially relative to binuclear species so that SMM properties can be degraded. Section 5.2 restates that more Ln ions make the coordination environment harder to control and the properties less pronounced.
scope: Multinuclear rare-earth SMMs beyond binuclear complexes.
caveats: This is a design limitation, not a claim that high-nuclearity clusters cannot be SMMs; specific Dy4, Dy5, and 4d-4f examples in the same section still show slow relaxation.
